legacy_cells.B: Radio Frequency Tagging–enabled patient monitoring: integrating mobility tracking with early warning systems for enhanced safety
legacy_cells.I: 033_2025_Radio Frequency Tagging–enabled patient monitoring integrating mobility tracking with early warning systems for enhanced safety.pdf
legacy_cells.S: Can patient location trajectories, combined with vital signs, detect abnormal movement or clinical risk early enough to alert staff?
legacy_cells.T: Simulated cohort of 150 patients observed for an average of 72 hours, spanning ambulatory, semi-ambulatory, immobile, post-surgery, geriatric, pediatric, ICU, and rehabilitation categories.
legacy_cells.V: Alert clinical staff to abnormal movement or elevated risk for timely intervention.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Radio Frequency Tagging (RFT) patient location/movement trajectories; physiological measurements (heart rate, respiration rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, temperature); activity labels
legacy_cells.AM: Weighted fusion of DTW mobility-anomaly scores and normalized Early Warning Score/vital-sign parameters into a composite risk score.
legacy_cells.AN: Interpolation was used to fill gaps in RFT readings; median filtering removed noise; mobility and physiological streams were timestamp-aligned.
legacy_cells.BL: One-second intervals for simulated RFT location trajectories.
legacy_cells.BN: Spatio-temporal Bayesian network with spatial dependencies and temporal dependencies on prior movement states.
legacy_cells.BS: DTW mobility-anomaly scores, a composite risk score, and threshold-triggered alerts; no generated future observations are reported.
legacy_cells.BT: DTW-based mobility anomaly detection and Early Warning Score/composite-risk alert output.
legacy_cells.BV: Spatio-temporal transition parameters estimated using maximum likelihood estimation or Bayesian inference; DTW anomaly scoring and weighted EWS risk scoring are also specified.
legacy_cells.DN: Simulated radio frequency tagging traces, MHEALTH, and PAMAP2.
legacy_cells.EG: Mean processing latency below 3 seconds per patient trajectory update; the text also reports a 1.8–2.8 minute average alert delay across categories.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with RFT-only monitoring; the paper reports 18–25% fewer missed anomalies and alerts 1.5–2 minutes faster on average.
legacy_cells.EO: Authors state identifiers were anonymised and the experiments used synthetic or publicly available data.
legacy_cells.ER: The paper states ethics approval and the Declaration of Helsinki guideline were not applicable.
legacy_cells.FB: Patient state is represented by location at time t and a sequence of estimated coordinates/locations over time, combined with physiological and activity observations.
legacy_cells.FL: RFT/WBAN sensing and timestamped preprocessing feed patient location and physiological/activity streams to a spatio-temporal Bayesian transition model and DTW anomaly detector; outputs are fused into a composite EWS risk score and threshold alerts. No planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors propose combining RFT mobility tracking with clinical scoring, a spatio-temporal Bayesian network for normal movement patterns, DTW anomaly detection, and integrated EWS alerts; they evaluate the framework on simulated hospital scenarios.
legacy_cells.FN: Abstract reports anomaly-detection accuracy of 87.5–91.0%, sensitivity of 88.4–96.2%, and F1 up to 93.5%; integrated-system tables report sensitivity of 91.7–97.5% and mean processing latency below 3 seconds per trajectory update.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors state that accuracy in other clinical contexts remains unverified and that patient turnover, workflow variation, and differing clinical scoring criteria may challenge implementation.
legacy_cells.FP: Authors call for evaluation on large real-life hospital data, integration of more sophisticated ML architectures such as deep reinforcement learning, and addition of wearable/biometric and multimodal data streams.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify a gap between RFID location tracking and early warning systems, stating that they are often separate and do not combine mobility information with clinical values for context-specific alerts.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper formulates a learned spatiotemporal movement-transition network and reports anomaly/EWS classification performance on hybrid data. It does not report separate future-state forecasting fidelity, free-running rollouts, intervention comparisons or prospective health outcomes. Core inclusion reflects the proposed learned temporal transition; demonstrated world-model capability remains unestablished.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M7 Outcome & causal layer; M9 Safety & governance
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Reuse the evaluated supporting estimator or audit behind a clear component boundary; validate its uncertainty and task limits again when connected to temporal dynamics.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pages 1–26: title/abstract/keywords; introduction and literature review; methods including data description, STBN modeling, RFT, monitoring workflow, DTW, EWS integration, and evaluation; results and Tables 1–8/Figures 1–10; discussion; limitations; future work; conclusion; declarations and data availability. References and publisher note also inspected. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Corrected D from the prefilled 2025 to 2026 because the PDF journal issue header identifies BioData Mining (2026) 19:2. Tables 5–8 are fragmented/misaligned in the extracted text, so table-specific metrics were not transcribed beyond values independently stated clearly in the abstract or body. The paper evaluates simulated/public-data anomaly and alert detection; it does not demonstrate action-conditioned treatment rollouts, causal identification, or prospective clinical benefit. Evidence QA: 40/60 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (66.7%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 62 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: L0 covers learned location-transition baseline/observed trajectory memory only. Persistent observed sequence need not be a posterior filter. Baseline generation/individualization unclear; anomaly metrics do not establish L1 forecasting.
notes: All26physicalPDFpages,8tablesand10figures reviewed. Revision 2 adjudication: learned hospital-location transition and retained observed patient trajectory satisfy implementation-stage core identity at L0 representation tier. No L1 future-state evaluation, counterfactual forecast or planner is established. BP_COMPONENT denotes representation/component contribution, not a clinically validated forecasting system. Exact baseline generation and patient-specific parameterization remain unclear. Header2026 differs from filename2025.
